text:
alex: quick ping — I opened a small terraform change to grant KMS access to billing-service's IRSA role in partner acct (123456789012). can someone sanity-check the grant + conditions?

maria: thanks for the heads up. can you paste the aws_kms_grant or key_policy snippet? want to make sure we don't accidentally allow broader principals.

alex: snippet from the branch: 
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "billing" {
  description = "billing key (cross-account for partner)"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Sid = "AllowAccountAdmin",
        Effect = "Allow",
        Principal = { AWS = "arn:aws:iam::555555555555:root" },
        Action = "kms:*",
        Resource = "*"
      }
    ]
  })
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "billing_irsa_grant" {
  name       = "billing-service-irsa-grant"
  key_id     = aws_kms_key.billing.id
  grantee_principal = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-billing-irsa"
  operations = ["Encrypt", "Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

leo: couple quick notes:
- prefer scoping key policy to deny broad root if possible. currently you allow the other account root for admins — that's ok if intentional but call it out in the PR description.
- for IRSA we typically grant to the _IAM role_ that the OIDC provider created (the role in partner acct). using grantee_principal as the role ARN is fine.
- add a condition on the grant or key policy to check `aws:PrincipalTag` or `aws:PrincipalArn` if you can, so only the service account principal can use it.

samir: small thing: partner runtime will call KMS from inside their EKS cluster, so recommend adding `aws:SourceAccount` in the key policy set to 123456789012 and also `kms:ViaService` if they're calling via an AWS service (not necessary in plain SDK calls).

maria: can you show the role trust policy on the partner side? the common pitfall is the role being assumable by wider principals if the OIDC condition is too loose.

alex: partner sent the role trust. relevant part: 
```json
{
  \"Effect\": \"Allow\",
  \"Principal\": {\"Federated\": \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.prod.example.com\"},
  \"Action\": \"sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity\",
  \"Condition\": {\"StringEquals\": {\"oidc.eks.prod.example.com:sub\": \"system:serviceaccount:billing-prod:billing-svc\"}}
}
```

leo: that looks good — sub is pretty tight. if you can also check the `aud` claim if the OIDC provider requires it.

maria: on the Terraform side, consider using `aws_kms_key.key.policy` to include the `Condition` with `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:PrincipalArn` as a belt-and-suspenders measure. grants are ephemeral and tied to the key, but the policy is the source of truth for access.

alex: makes sense. one more question — do we need `kms:GrantIsForAWSService` or `kms:ViaService` headers for SDK usage from pods? partner uses AWS SDK in-node (not via a service like S3) so I think no.

samir: correct, ViaService is for when requests are proxied through another AWS service. SDK direct calls don't need it.

maria: also think about session tag forwarding — partner's role is assumed via web identity, if they rely on tags for downstream checks make sure `sts:TagSession` is allowed in the trust. but not required for our grant.

alex: updated the PR: added `aws:SourceAccount` and an explicit `aws:PrincipalArn` condition. also narrowed the admin allow to a named admin role rather than root. pushing changes now, will run plan.

deployer-bot: terraform plan for branch alex/kms-billing returned: 
```
Plan: 1 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
+ aws_kms_grant.billing_irsa_grant
~ aws_kms_key.billing (policy changed)
```

maria: lgtm from infra side, leave the PR open until partner validates on their role side. can you add a note in the PR linking their role ARNs and the OIDC issuer?

alex: done. pinged partner for quick validation. once they confirm I'll request merge and schedule a small canary.

leo: sgtm. also add an entry in `infra/notes/kms-crossacct.md` describing the pattern we used (principal ARN + SourceAccount + OIDC-sub) so future folks don't widen it by accident.

alex: will add. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

samir: follow-up: partner validated and saw successful Decrypt call in their staging test. they didn't need session tags. you can roll forward.

alex: rolling out now, will watch logs and error rates. closing thread after stable canary. :rocket:
